# Project role

In this part of the project, you will build and test the conveyor system that
supplies workpieces to the robot cell. Visual Components (VC) represents the
physical plant: it creates products, transports them, and routes them at a
pusher conveyor. The completed conveyor model is later connected to the
[robot-cell project](robot_cell.qmd).

This page guides you through the work in the intended order. First make the
complete conveyor system work using VC's internal component behavior. Do not
begin with PLC communication. A working internal model gives you a known plant
before an external controller and communication delays are introduced.

The required version uses the standard Pusher Conveyor's internal routing
logic. When the conveyor is integrated with the robot cell, a PLC can later
command the ordinary conveyors without replacing this routing. PLC control of
the complete push cycle is a separate possible extension.

By completing this stage, you should be able to:

- create product types and generate a defined product mixture,
- assemble connected conveyor components,
- use component properties, behaviors, interfaces, and signals,
- configure and test product routing, and
- prepare a tested conveyor sublayout for integration with the robot cell.

# Required behavior

The conveyor system shall repeatedly perform the following material flow:

1. The Advanced Feeder creates blue, red, green, purple, and grey cylinders.
2. A shared run signal starts and stops the ordinary conveyor paths.
3. Blue, red, green, and purple cylinders are pushed onto a side conveyor.
4. Grey cylinders continue through the straight outlet toward the robot cell.

@fig-conveyor-flow summarizes both the product routes and the shared run
command. Product routing and control of the pusher's local path remain inside
the Pusher Conveyor in the required version.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-conveyor-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Required conveyor flow. The shared run signal controls the ordinary conveyors, while the Pusher Conveyor controls its local path and routes the products."
flowchart LR
    FEEDER[Advanced Feeder] --> IN[Incoming conveyor]
    IN --> PUSHER[Pusher Conveyor]
    PUSHER -->|grey cylinders| ROBOT[Robot-cell pickup conveyor]
    PUSHER -->|blue, red, green, purple| SIDE[Side conveyor]

    RUN[Shared run signal] -.-> IN
    RUN -.-> ROBOT
    RUN -.-> SIDE
```

For this first model, the side conveyor represents downstream storage with
unlimited capacity. You do not need to model storage limits or congestion after
a product has left the sorting conveyor.

The conveyor system does not use the VC Conveyor Motor component. Conveyor
motion is controlled through the conveyors' path signals, and conveyor fault
handling is not part of this stage.

# Components

Most components are found below `Models by Manufacturer > Visual Components`
in the eCatalog. If a category differs in your VC installation, search for the
stated component name.

| Quantity | Component | eCatalog subdirectory | Purpose |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 5 templates | Cylinder | `Basic Shapes` | Provide the geometry and material for the five product types. |
| 1 | Advanced Feeder | `Feeders` | Generate the product mixture. |
| As needed | Conveyor | `Conveyors` | Form the incoming, straight outgoing, and side transport paths. |
| 1 | Pusher Conveyor | `Conveyors` | Route selected products to the side conveyor. |
| 1 optional | Conveyor Sensor | `Conveyor Utilities` | Investigate colour detection and prepare for a possible later control extension. |

The [Layouts and components](visual_components.qmd#sec-vc-layouts-components),
[interfaces and signals](visual_components.qmd#sec-vc-interfaces), and
[products and production flow](visual_components.qmd#sec-vc-products-flow)
sections introduce the general VC concepts used below.

# Build and test in Visual Components

## Organize the conveyor sublayout {#sec-conveyor-sublayout}

Build the conveyor system in the VC file that will later contain the robot
cell. In the **Layouts** tab of the Cell Graph, create a sublayout named
`Conveyor system`. You can place components in the 3D world first and then use
**Move to Layout** to assign them to this sublayout.

Keep the downstream end accessible so that the robot cell can be connected
later.

## Create the product types

The product types define the identity and geometry of the items generated by
the feeder. A product's colour alone does not define a product type.

Create the five types as follows:

1. Add a Cylinder from `Basic Shapes` to the layout.
2. Set its material to the first required colour.
3. Open **Process > Product Type Editor** and select the plus button.
4. Name the new product type according to @tbl-conveyor-products.
5. In `ComponentUri`, use **Pick Component** and select the corresponding
   coloured cylinder.
6. Repeat the process for the other four colours.

| Product type | Material colour | Internal route |
|---|---|---|
| `Cylinder_blue` | Blue | Pusher outlet |
| `Cylinder_red` | Red | Pusher outlet |
| `Cylinder_green` | Green | Pusher outlet |
| `Cylinder_purple` | Purple | Pusher outlet |
| `Cylinder_grey` | Grey | Straight outlet |

: Conveyor product types and their required routes. {#tbl-conveyor-products}

Keep the five template cylinders away from the transport path. After
configuring the feeder, verify that the generated instances have the expected
product type and appearance.

## Configure the Advanced Feeder

Place an **Advanced Feeder** at the beginning of the incoming conveyor and
connect the compatible interfaces. In the feeder's component properties:

1. Set `CreationMode` to `Distribution`.
2. Open the `DistributionBook` tab.
3. Select **Open in Editor**.
4. Keep the first two column headings exactly as `ProductType` and
   `Probability`.
5. Enter the product types and probabilities from @tbl-feeder-distribution.

| Product type | Probability (%) |
|---|---:|
| `Cylinder_blue` | 23.75 |
| `Cylinder_red` | 23.75 |
| `Cylinder_green` | 23.75 |
| `Cylinder_purple` | 23.75 |
| `Cylinder_grey` | 5.00 |

: Initial feeder distribution. {#tbl-feeder-distribution}

The distribution is useful for repeated mixed-flow testing. While testing one
route, you may temporarily increase the probability of the relevant product
type instead of waiting for it to occur randomly. Restore the intended
distribution before validating the complete system.

## Assemble the transport path

Arrange the incoming conveyor, Pusher Conveyor, straight outgoing conveyor,
and side conveyor. Connect their compatible interfaces and check that the path
directions are consistent. The exact lengths and arrangement are design
choices, but leave enough straight path before the pusher for products to enter
its detection region reliably.

Run the simulation before configuring the routing. Confirm that products pass
from the feeder onto the incoming path and can move through each connected
conveyor without jumping, rotating unexpectedly, or becoming stuck at an
interface.

## Configure run control for the ordinary conveyors

Use one of the ordinary conveyors' existing Boolean `PowerOnSignal` values as
the shared run command:

1. Select an ordinary conveyor and show its component signals.
2. Draw signal connections from its `PowerOnSignal` to the `PowerOnSignal` of
   each remaining ordinary conveyor.
3. Use the selected conveyor's signal as the single run command for the line.

Change the shared value manually and verify that all connected paths start and
stop together. Test this again after resetting the simulation. Some component
behaviors react when a signal value changes, so explicitly toggle the command
once rather than assuming that its initial value has already been applied.

Do not connect this signal to the Pusher Conveyor's `One-WayPath`. Its internal
script temporarily stops and restarts that path while transferring a product.
Connecting another signal to the same `Enabled` property would create two
independent writers whose commands can overwrite one another.

The shared signal provides one clear line-level command for the ordinary
conveyors. It can later be mapped to the PLC without mapping those conveyors
separately.

## Configure internal pusher routing

The standard Pusher Conveyor contains internal logic that detects, attaches,
moves, and transfers a product to the selected outgoing path. Use that complete
behavior for the first project stage:

1. In the Pusher Conveyor properties, set `RouteBy` to `RoutingRule`.
2. Open the
   [`RoutingRule` editor](https://help.visualcomponents.com/5.1/Premium/en/English/Component%20Modeling/Behaviors/Material%20Flow/Routing_Rule.htm).
3. Select **Product Type Rule** as the routing rule.
4. Set the default connection to `Out`, the straight outlet.
5. Add `Cylinder_blue`, `Cylinder_red`, `Cylinder_green`, and
   `Cylinder_purple`, and assign each one to `Pusher`.
6. Leave `Cylinder_grey` on the default `Out` route.

Do not replace this behavior by controlling only the visible pusher joint. The
joint motion alone does not perform the product attachment and transfer between
conveyor paths.

Run the system until every product type has reached the pusher. Confirm that
the four coloured types leave through the side conveyor and that grey cylinders
continue through the straight outlet.

# Validate the internal model

Test the conveyor system incrementally and then run a longer mixed sequence.
Verify that:

- the feeder creates all five product types with the intended appearance,
- the shared run signal starts and stops every ordinary conveyor path,
- products cross each conveyor interface reliably,
- the pusher completes its full extension, transfer, and retraction sequence,
- coloured products enter the side path,
- grey products continue through the straight path, and
- resetting and restarting the simulation produces repeatable behavior.

Save this working version before adding the robot cell or external
communication. It becomes the known-working conveyor plant used in the next
project stage.

# Checkpoint before robot-cell integration

Before continuing to the robot cell, you should be able to demonstrate:

- the configured product types and feeder distribution,
- the complete conveyor layout in the `Conveyor system` sublayout,
- common start and stop behavior for the ordinary conveyors,
- correct internal routing for all five product types, and
- repeatable operation after a simulation reset.

Save a checkpoint copy of the layout and document the important component
settings and tests. Use this copy to return to the independently working
conveyor if a later integration change causes a problem.

# Connect the robot cell

Build the robot cell in the same VC file but initially leave space between the
two sublayouts. The [robot-cell instructions](robot_cell.qmd#sec-cell-sublayouts)
explain how to create the `Robot cell` sublayout and develop it with a copied
feeder that produces only grey cylinders. This avoids waiting for a rare grey
part while robot poses and motions are being tested. Keep the original feeder
and its mixed distribution unchanged; modify only the temporary copy in the
robot-cell sublayout.

After the robot-cell program works independently, follow
[Integrate the conveyor and robot-cell sublayouts](robot_cell.qmd#sec-cell-integrate)
to remove the temporary feeder and connect the straight conveyor outlet to the
robot pickup conveyor. Start the original mixed feeder again and confirm that
the sorting stage removes the coloured products while grey cylinders reach the
robot.

# External control boundary

The internally controlled pusher is the required and testable starting point.
The distinction between [internal VC control and external PLC
control](visual_components.qmd#sec-vc-external-control) is explained on the VC
page, while the
[PLC-integration section](simulation.qmd#sec-virtual-commissioning) explains the
wider purpose of connecting CODESYS and the simulation.

In the robot cell's external-control stage, the shared `PowerOnSignal` can be
mapped to CODESYS so that the PLC starts and stops the ordinary conveyors.
Product routing and the pusher's local path control remain internal to VC. This
adds PLC line control without introducing another pusher state machine.

## Possible extension: PLC-controlled pushing

Full PLC control of the push cycle requires a tested interface that requests
one complete transfer and receives completion feedback. Directly commanding
the pusher joint is not sufficient.

Full PLC control of the push cycle is not part of the required stage. If it is
assigned as an extension, you will receive a prepared VC interface, its I/O
contract, and acceptance tests before implementation.

## Optional signal investigations

The internally routed model does not require an external colour signal. The
following investigations are relevant only if you want to inspect the
component in more detail or if a later PLC extension is assigned.

To expose the Pusher Conveyor's built-in product detector as a Boolean signal:

1. Add a `BooleanSignal` behavior named `PartDetected`.
2. Open the `ComponentPathSensor` behavior.
3. Set its `BoolSignal` property to `PartDetected`.
4. Run products through the pusher and verify the signal transition.

You can also investigate the **Conveyor Sensor** component's RGB detection:

1. Add the sensor to an ordinary conveyor and reset the simulation.
2. Open the sensor's `RGB` properties and enable colour detection.
3. Place one of the coloured template cylinders inside the detection area.
4. Select **Teach in color 1**.
5. Repeat for the remaining colours and observe the resulting outputs.

The RGB sensor reads the simulated material in its detection area, not the
product-type name. Therefore, verify its outputs with products generated by the
feeder before using them in control logic. RGB detection does not replace the
product-type routing used in the required model.
